events.title: Traditional date of the martyrdom of Saint Valentine
events.description: Tradition holds that Valentine, a priest or bishop of Terni, was beheaded on the Via Flaminia outside Rome. His link with romantic love dates only from the Middle Ages, notably the poetry of Chaucer.
events.html: Tradition holds that Valentine, a priest or bishop of Terni, was beheaded on the Via Flaminia outside Rome. His link with romantic love dates only from the Middle Ages, notably the poetry of Chaucer.

events.title: Oaths of Strasbourg sworn by Charlemagne's grandsons
events.description: Louis the German and Charles the Bald pledged alliance against their brother Lothair, each swearing in the other's language. The oaths are the earliest surviving text in a form of French.
events.html: Louis the German and Charles the Bald pledged alliance against their brother Lothair, each swearing in the other's language. The oaths are the earliest surviving text in a form of French.

events.title: Deposed Richard II dies at Pontefract Castle
events.description: Richard II, overthrown by his cousin Henry Bolingbroke in 1399, died in captivity around this date, probably starved to death. His fall sowed the dynastic rivalry behind the Wars of the Roses.
events.html: Richard II, overthrown by his cousin Henry Bolingbroke in 1399, died in captivity around this date, probably starved to death. His fall sowed the dynastic rivalry behind the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: Captain James Cook is killed in Hawaii
events.description: Cook died in a clash with Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay after trying to take a chief hostage over a stolen boat. His three voyages had charted much of the Pacific.
events.html: Cook died in a clash with Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay after trying to take a chief hostage over a stolen boat. His three voyages had charted much of the Pacific.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell files his telephone patent
events.description: Bell's lawyer filed his application at the US Patent Office on the same day that Elisha Gray filed a caveat for a similar device. Bell's patent was granted in March and upheld in long litigation.
events.html: Bell's lawyer filed his application at the US Patent Office on the same day that Elisha Gray filed a caveat for a similar device. Bell's patent was granted in March and upheld in long litigation.

events.title: Saint Valentine's Day Massacre in Chicago
events.description: Gunmen, some dressed as police, shot dead seven men linked to Bugs Moran's gang in a garage. The killings, widely blamed on Al Capone, turned public opinion against gangland violence.
events.html: Gunmen, some dressed as police, shot dead seven men linked to Bugs Moran's gang in a garage. The killings, widely blamed on Al Capone, turned public opinion against gangland violence.

events.title: ENIAC is unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania
events.description: The US Army publicly revealed ENIAC, the first programmable general-purpose electronic computer. With nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, it could perform 5,000 additions a second.
events.html: The US Army publicly revealed ENIAC, the first programmable general-purpose electronic computer. With nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, it could perform 5,000 additions a second.

events.title: Ayatollah Khomeini issues a fatwa against Salman Rushdie
events.description: Iran's leader called on Muslims to kill the author of 'The Satanic Verses' and his publishers. Rushdie spent years in hiding; translators and publishers were attacked, and he was stabbed in 2022.
